keyFindings.description: It reads 'plus this round's local checks at the forward-merge head 9dae22b7'. 9dae22b7 is round two's forward merge, from 2026-10-23; this round's is b2350b438c51d67f4d1f5583ddce602ad50851ea, from 2026-10-24, and the body's own E2E (tester) line names that one. So the field a human reads first states that this round's checks ran at a head two rounds old. skills/legion-worker/references/pr-body.md makes the brief the human's and a stale line a finding against the implementer rather than a line a later role rewrites, and a claim about which head was checked is exactly the class this pull request deletes. Name this round's merge, or drop the clause.

keyFindings.file: .legion/INFRA-83/test.json, the sweep proof's surface and command
keyFindings.description: The proof's surface reads 'the staged skills, bundle, prompts and docs/solutions read for new text'; its command greps 'over skills, the bundle and the prompts'. docs/solutions is named in the surface and absent from the command, so the corpus was not read. The gap is not hypothetical: the merge added five docs/solutions files, and one of them - docs/solutions/legion/the-pull-request-body-is-shared-state-read-it-back-before-you-claim-you-changed-it-INFRA-149.md, status active, module legion-worker - names the deleted CI line twice. I read all five myself: only that one mentions it, and under the architect's round-four rule (an instruction to write the line gets a supersede note, a dated narration keeps its text) it narrates - the mentions are an example inside a lesson about partly-true claims and a record of what happened on sjawhar/legion#2143 - so the corpus is clean and that file rightly keeps its text. What is not clean is a proof whose surface names a corpus its command never touched: it cannot be re-derived by the reader it exists for, which is this issue's own subject. Make the claim match the command, or run the read.

The file a worker is sent to before it writes the trailer states the path rule unconditionally under '## The shape GitHub honours', and INFRA-149's correcting sentence - that retro's push never carries the line whatever paths it touches - sits sixteen lines later under '## Every other push carries no such line', a heading a retro worker whose push is .legion/-only has every reason to skip. In the four texts main pinned the two sit adjacent. Mitigated, since skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md and prompts/roles/implementer.md both state it and retro runs as the implementer role, so I rate it minor; the fix is one pointer clause in the first section and never a second copy, since the pin asserts exactly one occurrence per file.
